checks: For a line meeting the interior of one planar body there are at most two boundary intersection points. The angular normal-cone interior of each such point has zero curvature; its finitely many endpoint angles and a supporting segment's facet normal are null for the nonatomic part. Radon–Nikodym positivity on the active coordinates transfers the null-set statement to R.

The BV chain rule for epsilon arctan(u/epsilon) handles both the diffuse part and the countable jumps. The jump terms converge to zero in variation by their summable upper bound, while the diffuse multiplier converges to 1_{u=0}. On a Jensen zero set, at every non-jump differentiability point u=g'_a is zero by nonnegativity. This gives the claimed exact diffuse locality and r∈L.

Upper semicontinuity of the exposed face and continuity of the inactive gaps give an open neighborhood for each strict pattern. Rational guards and compact subintervals cover the pattern, and (1/k)R restricted where every positive r_z≥1/k is dominated by all affected full curvature measures.

The nonzero nonatomic source has positive mass in the guard interior and can be split into |P|+3 positive pieces. Two endpoint constraints and |P| mass constraints give a nonzero bounded density, whose sine Green potential is C^1 and satisfies φ''+φ=ψν. Poincaré on a guard shorter than π gives strictly negative quadratic area, so the stated normalization is possible.

Curvature stays nonnegative for both signs by domination and bounded density. The active rows have zero algebraic variation for all angles, while inactive rows have a positive guard margin. Periodic smoothing with nonnegative curvature proves actual support feasibility and retains the original inballs up to a fixed shrinkage.

The global support area formula gives zero first derivatives and second derivative −v_z². In a changed guard, the two face endpoints shift by t v_z(φu+φ'u'), preserving strict membership even at atom angles. The common outside arc cancels in the closed winding path, which has zero winding in the other halfplane; hence the cap area change is exactly the indicated bit times the full area change.

Source c7a0c159c6cf35f0 §§2–3 supplies the arbitrary-pattern scope; 181e74b2f3c435dc §1 and ed7be0e1efdfe13b §§2–4 supply the re-proved locality and Green steps. The stronger stress conclusions from the rest of those notes are outside this lemma.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use the one-dimensional BV chain rule with a bounded BV derivative u, and C^1 function T_epsilon with globally bounded derivative. The diffuse contribution uses the precise representative and the jump uses the two one-sided traces.
dependencies.reference: A. I. Vol'pert, The spaces BV and quasilinear equations, §5

overlap.comparison: Its support-function and area identities are reusable background, but it assumes a common guarded interval with mutually comparable nonatomic curvature and a tensor independence condition for exact area-preserving polygonization. It does not cover arbitrary diffuse contact strata or the signed second-order generators.
Its rank-one polygonization also assumes common interval structure and aims to keep areas exactly constant. It does not supply these countably guarded signed variations on arbitrary diffuse strata.

readability: In the pattern subscript, j ranges over the fixed caps and z ranges over the active fiber set J. This is clear in the argument and avoids conflating the two index sets.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen theorem and proof, source-locator and dependency comparison at the pinned graph, and exact arithmetic on the illustrative constructions where relevant.
summary: The diffuse-curvature strata admit the claimed countable guarded sources and exact two-sided compatible variations, with the stated second total and cap area derivatives.
